builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries
summary: Replaces the need for every project to build custom extraction pipelines to convert MIMIC-IV free-text discharge summaries into structured tables. Costs are low for the reader because the output is a pre-computed dataset; the authors absorbed the LLM inference and engineering expense, though integrating a new schema requires effort. Schema-guided LLM extraction can hallucinate or misclassify clinical entities, and the 8% error rate may require manual verification for high-stakes applications.
rationale: The dataset eliminates redundant pipeline development and provides immediately usable structured data within the reader's infrastructure constraints.

claims.statement: Replaces the need for every project to build custom extraction pipelines to convert MIMIC-IV free-text discharge summaries into structured tables. Costs are low for the reader because the output is a pre-computed dataset; the authors absorbed the LLM inference and engineering expense, though integrating a new schema requires effort. Schema-guided LLM extraction can hallucinate or misclassify clinical entities, and the 8% error rate may require manual verification for high-stakes applications.
Yields 10 times more patient-history entries and medication histories for more than twice as many admissions; medical validation reports extraction accuracy above 92%.
